name: Quicklarity
description: AI-Powered Strategic Planning - Production-ready MVP with Clerk/Supabase/Stripe/PostHog/Notion integrations

gpt_4o_nano.note: Used for profile normalization, doc summarization (cheapest)

gpt_4o_mini.note: Used for free users' final plan (crucial step)

gpt_4o.note: Used for paid users' final plan (highest quality)

baseline_assumption.note: Conservative estimate for cost cap validation

profile_normalization.description: Normalize founder profile into structured summary

doc_summarization_per_chunk.description: Summarize one document chunk (800 tokens + prompt overhead)

final_plan_free_user.description: Generate strategic plan JSON (free tier, uses better model for crucial step)

final_plan_paid_user.description: Generate strategic plan JSON (paid tier, highest quality)

rectifier_if_needed.description: Single attempt to fix malformed JSON (rarely needed)

free_user.mitigation: Using gpt-4o-nano for cheap ops and gpt-4o-mini for crucial final plan. Cost is $0.001 < $0.05 cap (2% utilization).
free_user.breakdown: Profile (400 tok, nano) + 1 Doc (1200 tok, nano) + Final Plan (1000 tok, mini) + Rectifier (400 tok, nano) = 3000 tokens max

paid_user.mitigation: Using gpt-4o for paid users' final plan (highest quality). Total cost $0.023 is 2.3% of $1.00 cap.
paid_user.breakdown: Profile (400 tok, nano) + 3 Docs (3600 tok, nano) + Final Plan (2000 tok, gpt-4o) + Rectifier (400 tok, nano) = 6400 tokens max

notes: With GPT-4o family (nano/mini/full), both tiers are well within budget.
Free user: $0.001 actual vs $0.05 cap (2% utilization) - uses gpt-4o-nano + gpt-4o-mini
Paid user: $0.023 actual vs $1.00 cap (2.3% utilization) - uses gpt-4o-nano + gpt-4o
Free users get gpt-4o-mini for crucial final plan step (better quality than old gpt-3.5)
Paid users get full gpt-4o for final plan (highest quality available)
Rule-based scoring saves $0.05-0.10 per user vs LLM-based scoring.

free_users: Limited to 1 document chunk max (vs 3 for paid)
Max final plan tokens: 600 (vs 1200 for paid)
Rule-based scoring eliminates separate LLM scoring call
paid_users: Uses gpt-4o-mini (cheaper than gpt-4o, 94% cheaper than gpt-4)
Rule-based scoring eliminates separate LLM scoring call
Single final LLM call (no iterative refinement)
both_tiers: Document summaries cached by SHA256 hash (eliminates duplicate processing)
Rectifier only called once if JSON parse fails (not iterative)
All token limits enforced via max_tokens parameter
Budget guards in worker code prevent runaway costs
